What I work on

I build systems where a model may propose but a deterministic check decides what gets admitted, and where the system says so out loud when it cannot support an answer. GIN is the frame. SEAR and Receipts with Assay are slices of it. Latch tested GIN's gate idea on small-model reasoning.

Some of it held on small sets. Some of it failed under criteria I wrote down before running it. Both sides are below, with the same weight, and each line links to its evidence.

Source: framing written for this site from the ledger entries it links to; 'GIN is the frame' and the slice list follow the author's vault note CALICHE/Projects/GIN/GIN.md; the Latch sentence follows Latch docs/HISTORY.md at cdcd512.

gin-divergence-realtextGINMEASUREDLINKED STALE2026-07-05On six two-node queries over excerpts of public institutional and advocacy texts, the no-continuation arm kept both sides of each divergence and fabricated nothing, with Mistral-7B and with Qwen2.5-7B.Generality. gin-nc-baselineGINMEASUREDLINKED STALE2026-07-02On a 20-query synthetic eval set, SEAR's no-continuation arm produced no fabricated claims, while a plain RAG arm on the same set fabricated about a quarter of its claims.Performance on real-world corpora (this set is synthetic and author-built).
